findings.detail: Neither citation mentions CARD9: PMID:38716725 names integrin alpha X only in an inferred mesangial cell-macrophage ligand-receptor axis, and rs11574637 is a variant-IgAN GWAS row.
PMID:33052226 (review abstract on mucosal immunity and gut microbiome in IgAN) names neither CARD9 nor TNFSF13/APRIL, and rs4077515 is a CARD9 missense-IgAN GWAS row that says nothing about TNFSF13.

None of the three citations says CFH inhibits complement: the Open Targets score and the rs6677604 GWAS row tie CFH to IgAN only, and PMID:36316518 infers complement activation from retinal drusen without mentioning CFH.

The only citation for 'complement cascade increases iC3b' is a Reactome over-representation of 'Complement cascade' in the run's own input gene list (2 of 163 entities, FDR 0.03), which is circular and never mentions iC3b.
PMID:38716725 reports a scRNA-seq inferred ITGAX/ITGAM/C3 interaction axis between mesangial cells and macrophages; it names C3, not iC3b, and reports no binding.

The HPA record (DEFA4 RNA enriched in bone marrow and neutrophil progenitors) is cited for 'neutrophil degranulation increases DEFA4'; expression in progenitors says nothing about release by degranulation.
Not one of the run's 16 citation slots states its step, so every statement has empty evidence.

Every step that reaches the disease or glomerular injury has polarity 'unknown', though the mechanisms state a direction ('drives', 'exacerbating', 'promotes ... accelerating the progression'), so no hypothesis composes from gene to disease.
Seven of the 16 citation slots are GWAS Catalog variant-IgAN rows used for gene-level mechanism steps; each names an allele and the disease, never the step's other end or the gene's direction.
rs2738058 is intergenic, 25.8 kb from DEFA4 with DEFA9P/DEFA10P closest, and the study's author-reported gene is 'DEFA' (the cluster), yet the run attributes the signal to DEFA4.
rs11574637 lies in an ITGAX intron, but the study reports the locus for both ITGAM and ITGAX (ITGAM starts 24.7 kb away), so the signal is not ITGAX's alone; the run reads it as ITGAX only.
'Glomerular injury leads_to IgA glomerulonephritis' makes a defining feature of a glomerulonephritis (MONDO: inflammation of glomeruli) its cause.
The mechanism runs TNFSF13 -> IgA class switching -> poorly O-galactosylated IgA1 -> IgAN, but the chain jumps from TNFSF13 straight to IgAN; the intermediate nodes are never steps.
The mechanism puts ITGAX on infiltrating glomerular macrophages driving local inflammation, but the chain has no inflammation or macrophage-activation node between 'iC3b binds ITGAX' and IgAN.
supporting_evidence and contradicting_evidence are empty for all three hypotheses, and sources.json has no 'supporting' or 'contradicting' citation, so no counter-evidence was sought.

The OR4X1/ZNF174 abstention cites 'GWAS:OR4X1:no-association', 'GWAS:ZNF174:no-association' and 'STRING:no-edges', none of which is in sources.json, and says Open Targets found no association without citing any OT record.

The run gave CURIEs for 3 of its 10 chain nodes (CARD9 as ENSEMBL, DEFA4 as UniProtKB, IgAN as MONDO:0005342); ITGAX, TNFSF13, CFH, complement cascade, iC3b, neutrophil degranulation, glomerular injury and the gut, macrophage and kidney contexts had empty CURIEs.
All three hypotheses are labelled low confidence and 'speculative', which matches the curation: no citation states any step.

The corpus has no term for iC3b itself (GO has only the functions 'iC3b binding' and 'iC3b receptor activity'), so iC3b is grounded to its parent, PR:000019178 complement C3 proteolytic cleavage product; intact C3 cannot stand in because complement activation raises its fragments while consuming C3.
'Glomerular injury' has no exact term; HP:0100820 Glomerulopathy, defined as 'diseases affecting the glomeruli', is the nearest and is S7's target.

A variant-to-gene link (rs4077515 and rs3803800 are missense in CARD9 and TNFSF13, rs6677604 intronic in CFH): with no such form, the run's only genetic support for each gene is excluded whole and leaves no trace in the arms.
The run's abstention (OR4X1 and ZNF174: no shared mechanism, 'grounded') is a claim of absence with its own evidence, and curated.json has no place for it.

For leads_to with polarity unknown, the guide lets only a cited text supply the sign, not the run's own mechanism, and 'leads to glomerular injury' sits between that rule and the 'undirected change' rule; the audit applied the undirected-change rule to h3_defa4.2 (pos on glomerulopathy, S7) and no_sign to the three steps that end at the disease.
H1.2 has context gut and H1.3 has none, so the refinement the guide asks for makes H1.2's object (TNFSF13 in intestine) a different node from H1.3's subject, a break the run did not intend.

'Exacerbating IgA glomerulonephritis' fits both severity ('aggravates') and progression ('exacerbation') in the aspect table; the curator chose severity, the audit progression, because the table names 'exacerbation' and the object is the disease, not a feature.

The title ('Intestinal ITGAX+ antigen-presenting cells'), mechanism ('ITGAX (CD11c) positive dendritic cells') and falsification ('Itgax+ dendritic cells') use ITGAX as a cell marker, but H1.1 makes the ITGAX gene the activator of CARD9, a molecular step nothing in the run states.

The title says iC3b 'hyperactivates ITGAX+ myeloid cells', but H2.3 is 'iC3b binds ITGAX' with polarity unknown; a binding carries no direction, so even a signed H2.4 would leave CFH with no route to IgAN.

The one-line GWAS summaries the agent saw name a single gene ('mapped gene DEFA4' for rs2738058, 'author-reported gene ITGAX' for rs11574637), while the records show an intergenic variant whose nearest genes are DEFA9P/DEFA10P (DEFA1 13.6 kb, DEFA4 25.8 kb; author gene 'DEFA') and a locus reported for ITGAM and ITGAX.

audit.after: statement S7: DEFA4 →+ phenotype glomerularInjury (HP:0100820), sign_note, evidence [], same two exclusions; H3 note and the approximate_term and rule_missing findings updated
audit.reason: the guide's undirected-change rule covers 'leads to abnormal X' with no sign: if an HP/MP term for the abnormal state exists, the step is an effect, pos, on it. Glomerular injury is an abnormal state and the curator had already grounded it to HP:0100820. The leads_to-unknown rule still governs the steps that end at the disease (H1.3, H2.4, H3.3). No route changes: H3.3 stays unsigned
